doc.title: Peter Erskine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 9, 2020

title: Joining the Stan Kenton band at 18
summary: Rowe reads a review of Kenton's Birthday in Britain mentioning the unknown Erskine; Erskine calls the band a great school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well I wonder if you have a memory of this — this was a comment, this actually, from one of those jazz on CD books which probably came out in the late 90s but the person was talking about “Birthday in Britain 1973,” a Kenton LP. And his comment was, “This 19-piece band is mostly filled with forgotten youngsters except for Willie Maiden and Dick Scherer and the then-unknown drummer Peter Erskine.” So you’ve come a long way.
The Kenton band was a great school, it was a great doorway into playing. I mean I haven’t forgotten any of the other youngsters that were in the band.
But you were 18 is that right?
